variants.stem: Which part of the brain coordinates balance and smooth voluntary movement?
Damage to which brain structure would most likely cause clumsy, uncoordinated movements?
Which region of the brain fine-tunes muscle activity and helps maintain posture?
Which brain structure is located at the back of the skull beneath the occipital lobes and controls coordination?
Which part of the brain is primarily responsible for balance and motor coordination?
A person has trouble walking in a straight line and touching their nose with a finger. Which brain structure is likely affected?
Which structure compares intended movements with actual movements to keep them smooth?
The brain region most involved in coordinating muscle timing and equilibrium is the:

questions.why: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movement, posture, and balance.
questions.deep: Cerebrum = thinking, sensation, voluntary movement planning; medulla = breathing and heart rate; thalamus = sensory relay. Memory aid: cerebellum is the 'little brain' tucked below the cerebrum.

variants.stem: Which neurotransmitter is released by motor neurons at the neuromuscular junction?
Skeletal muscle contraction is triggered by which neurotransmitter?
Which chemical messenger crosses the synapse between a motor neuron and a muscle fiber?
At the junction between a motor neuron and a skeletal muscle cell, the neuron releases which neurotransmitter?
Which neurotransmitter binds to receptors on the muscle cell membrane to start a muscle action potential?
Which neurotransmitter is cleared from the neuromuscular junction by the enzyme cholinesterase?
Which neurotransmitter is the main one used by the somatic nervous system to stimulate muscles?
A motor neuron signals a muscle to contract by releasing which neurotransmitter?

questions.why: Motor neurons release acetylcholine, which binds receptors on the muscle fiber and triggers contraction.
questions.deep: Acetylcholinesterase then breaks acetylcholine down so the signal ends. Dopamine is tied to reward and movement control in the brain, serotonin to mood, and GABA is the main inhibitory neurotransmitter.

variants.stem: What is the effect of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) on the kidneys?
When ADH levels rise, the kidneys will:
A dehydrated person releases more ADH. What happens in the kidneys?
Antidiuretic hormone acts on the collecting ducts to cause the kidneys to:
Which kidney response is stimulated by ADH from the posterior pituitary?
How does ADH help the body conserve fluid?
Increased ADH secretion results in the kidneys doing which of the following?
ADH makes the urine more concentrated because the kidneys:

questions.why: ADH increases the water permeability of the collecting ducts, so more water is reabsorbed and urine is more concentrated.
questions.deep: ADH is made in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary. 'Anti-diuretic' means against producing lots of urine. Alcohol suppresses ADH, which is why it makes you urinate more.

variants.stem: Which of the following is an example of passive immunity?
A newborn is protected by antibodies delivered through breast milk. This is an example of:
Which situation provides passive immunity?
Passive immunity occurs when a person receives which of the following?
Which option describes temporary protection given by ready-made antibodies from another source?
Which of these gives immediate but short-lived protection because the body did not make the antibodies itself?
An infant receives antibodies that crossed the placenta from the mother. Which type of immunity is this?
Which of the following is NOT active immunity?

questions.why: Passive immunity comes from antibodies made by someone else (for example, mother to infant), so it is immediate but temporary.
questions.deep: Active immunity (from infection or vaccination) means your own B cells make antibodies and memory cells, and it lasts much longer. Passive immunity does not create memory cells.

variants.stem: Which gland produces cortisol?
The stress hormone cortisol is secreted by which part of the body?
Which structure releases glucocorticoids such as cortisol in response to ACTH?
ACTH from the pituitary stimulates which gland to release cortisol?
Chronic stress raises blood levels of a hormone made by which structure?
Cortisol, which raises blood glucose and suppresses inflammation, comes from the:
Which endocrine tissue is the source of cortisol?
Which of the following produces cortisol?

questions.why: The adrenal cortex secretes cortisol (a glucocorticoid), along with aldosterone and sex hormones.
questions.deep: The adrenal medulla (inner part) makes epinephrine and norepinephrine for fight-or-flight. The cortex makes steroid hormones. Pathway: hypothalamus (CRH) → pituitary (ACTH) → adrenal cortex (cortisol).

variants.stem: Which structure lies between the pharynx and the trachea and contains the vocal cords?
Air moving from the pharynx toward the trachea passes through which structure?
Which part of the airway houses the vocal folds?
The voice box is the common name for which structure?
Which structure is located just above the trachea and below the pharynx?
Sound is produced when air passes over the vocal cords in which structure?
Which respiratory structure is protected by the epiglottis during swallowing?
Which airway structure connects the pharynx to the trachea?

questions.why: The larynx connects the pharynx to the trachea and contains the vocal cords.
questions.deep: Air path: nose → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli. The esophagus runs behind the trachea and carries food to the stomach.

variants.stem: Which muscle tissue is both striated and involuntary?
Which type of muscle is found only in the heart wall?
Intercalated discs are a feature of which muscle type?
Which muscle tissue contracts rhythmically without conscious control and appears striped under a microscope?
Which muscle tissue is found only in the walls of the heart chambers?
Which muscle type forms the myocardium?
Which tissue has striations, one or two nuclei per cell, and branched fibers?
Which type of muscle contracts automatically to pump blood?

questions.why: Cardiac muscle is striated like skeletal muscle but involuntary, with intercalated discs linking branched cells.
questions.deep: Skeletal = striated, voluntary, attached to bones. Smooth = non-striated, involuntary, found in walls of organs and vessels. Cardiac = striated, involuntary, heart only.

variants.stem: Which cell fragments form a plug to start blood clotting?
Which blood component is involved in forming a platelet plug at a damaged vessel?
After a cut, which blood elements stick together at the injury site to begin stopping the bleeding?
Which formed elements of blood are fragments of megakaryocytes?
Which blood component initiates clotting by clumping at a wound?
A low count of which blood element could cause excessive bleeding?
Thrombocytes are also known as:
Which of the following initiates hemostasis by aggregating at a break in a blood vessel?

questions.why: Platelets (thrombocytes) are cell fragments that aggregate at an injury and help form a clot.
questions.deep: Erythrocytes carry oxygen, neutrophils engulf bacteria, lymphocytes (B and T cells) run adaptive immunity. Platelets come from megakaryocytes in bone marrow.

variants.stem: Which of the following are functions of the skeletal system? Select all that apply.
Select every function performed by bones and the skeletal system.
Which options are roles of the skeleton? Select all that apply.
Identify all functions of the skeletal system from the list.
Which of these does the skeletal system do? Select all that apply.
Select all tasks carried out by the skeleton.
Which of the following are correct functions of bones? Select all that apply.
Choose every function that belongs to the skeletal system.

questions.why: Bones support the body, protect organs, make blood cells in marrow, and store minerals such as calcium and phosphorus.
questions.deep: They also act as levers for movement. Digestive enzymes are secreted by glands and the lining of the digestive tract, not bone.

variants.stem: Tap the axon.
Which part of the neuron conducts impulses away from the cell body? Tap it.
Locate the long fiber that carries electrical signals away from the soma and tap it.
On this neuron diagram, tap the axon.
Tap the part of the neuron that transmits the action potential toward the axon terminals.
Find the structure that carries an impulse from the cell body toward the next cell and tap it.
Tap the portion of the neuron that is insulated by myelin segments.
Tap the neuron's long projection that sends signals outward.

questions.why: The axon is the long fiber (here wrapped in myelin segments) that carries action potentials away from the cell body.
questions.deep: Dendrites (the branching ends on the left) receive signals and conduct them toward the cell body; the axon sends them away to the axon terminals, which release neurotransmitter. Myelin speeds conduction along the axon.

variants.stem: Which molecule forms the basic structure of the cell membrane?
The cell membrane is built mainly from a double layer of which molecules?
Which type of molecule makes up the bilayer of a cell membrane?
A phospholipid bilayer is the main framework of which cell structure?
Which molecules have hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic tails and line up to form the cell membrane?
The fluid mosaic model describes a membrane made mostly of which molecule type?
Which biomolecule is the primary structural component of plasma membranes?
Which of the following forms the main framework of cellular membranes?

questions.why: Cell membranes are built from a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins and cholesterol.
questions.deep: Hydrophilic (water-loving) heads face the watery inside and outside; hydrophobic (water-fearing) tails face each other in the middle. Cellulose is a plant cell wall component.

variants.stem: What is the term for the diffusion of water across a semipermeable membrane?
Water moves from an area of low solute concentration to an area of high solute concentration across a membrane. This process is called:
Which process moves water through a membrane toward the side with more dissolved solute?
A red blood cell placed in salt water shrinks as water leaves it. Which process is responsible?
Which transport process specifically involves the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane?
Which process requires no energy and moves water down its concentration gradient?
Plant roots take up water from soil mainly through which process?
The movement of solvent across a membrane to balance solute concentration is known as:

questions.why: Osmosis is the passive diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane toward higher solute concentration.
questions.deep: In a hypotonic solution cells swell, in hypertonic they shrink, in isotonic there is no net water movement. Active transport uses ATP to move solutes against their gradient.

variants.stem: How many nucleotides make up one mRNA codon?
A codon is a sequence of how many mRNA bases that codes for one amino acid?
Each amino acid is specified by a codon made of how many nucleotides?
The genetic code is read in groups of how many nucleotides?
How many bases are in the codon that tRNA's anticodon pairs with?
A triplet code means each codon contains how many nucleotides?
If an mRNA strand is 30 nucleotides long, each codon within it is made of how many nucleotides?
What is the number of nucleotides in a single codon?

questions.why: A codon is three nucleotides long and codes for one amino acid (or a start/stop signal).
questions.deep: With 4 bases and 3 positions there are 4³ = 64 possible codons for just 20 amino acids, so the code is redundant. AUG is the start codon; UAA, UAG, and UGA are stop codons.

variants.stem: What is the term for an individual with two identical alleles for a gene?
An organism with the genotype AA or aa is described as:
Which term describes a genotype with two copies of the same allele?
If both alleles at a gene locus are the same, the organism is said to be:
Which word describes the genotype TT?
A pea plant carries two copies of the allele for purple flowers (PP). Its genotype is:
Which term applies when an individual inherited the same allele from each parent?
The genotype tt is described as:

questions.why: Having two identical alleles for a gene is called homozygous.
questions.deep: Homo = same, hetero = different. Homozygous dominant (AA), homozygous recessive (aa), heterozygous (Aa). Hemizygous refers to a single copy of a gene, as with X-linked genes in males.

variants.stem: A DNA sample is 30% adenine. What percent of the DNA is guanine? Type a number.
In a double-stranded DNA molecule, 30% of the bases are adenine. What percent are guanine? Type a number.
If thymine makes up 30% of a DNA sample, what percent is cytosine? Type a number.
A scientist finds that 30% of the nucleotides in a DNA sample are adenine. Give the percent of guanine nucleotides as a number.
DNA is double stranded and contains 30% adenine. What percentage is guanine? Type a number.
Given that 30% of a DNA molecule's bases are adenine, what percent of its bases are guanine? Type a number.
A double helix contains 30% thymine. Type the percent of the bases that are guanine.
Using base-pairing rules, if adenine is 30% of a DNA sample, what percent is guanine? Type a number.

questions.why: A pairs with T, so A = T = 30% (60% total). The remaining 40% is split equally between G and C, giving 20% each.
questions.deep: Chargaff's rules: in double-stranded DNA, A = T and G = C, and all four bases add up to 100%.

variants.stem: Which of the following are found in eukaryotic cells but not in prokaryotic cells? Select all that apply.
Select every structure that is present in eukaryotes and absent in bacteria.
Which options are membrane-bound structures found only in eukaryotic cells? Select all that apply.
Identify all structures that distinguish eukaryotic cells from prokaryotic cells.
Which of these would you expect in an animal cell but not in a bacterial cell? Select all that apply.
Select all organelles or structures that bacteria lack but eukaryotes have.
Which of the following are unique to eukaryotes? Select all that apply.
Choose every structure that a prokaryotic cell does not have but a eukaryotic cell does.

questions.why: Eukaryotes have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria and the Golgi apparatus. Ribosomes and a plasma membrane are found in both cell types.
questions.deep: Prokaryotes (bacteria and archaea) have DNA in a nucleoid region, no membrane-bound organelles, and smaller ribosomes, but they do have ribosomes and a plasma membrane.

variants.stem: Which element is the most electronegative?
Which of the following elements attracts electrons most strongly in a bond?
Which element has the highest electronegativity on the periodic table?
In a bond between hydrogen and which of these elements would the electrons be pulled most strongly toward the other atom?
Which element is most likely to pull shared electrons toward itself?
Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group. Which element listed is the most electronegative?
Which of the following has the greatest tendency to attract bonding electrons?
Which element is at the top of the electronegativity scale?

questions.why: Fluorine is the most electronegative element.
questions.deep: Electronegativity trend: increases left to right across a period and bottom to top within a group, so fluorine (top right, excluding noble gases) is highest, followed by oxygen.

questions.deep: Water is polar because oxygen pulls electrons more strongly than hydrogen. Hydrogen bonds cause cohesion, high surface tension, high specific heat, and ice floating on water.

variants.stem: What is the term for the change from a solid directly to a gas?
Dry ice turns directly into carbon dioxide gas without becoming a liquid. This process is called:
Which phase change skips the liquid state when going from solid to gas?
Snow slowly disappearing on a cold, dry, sunny day without melting is an example of:
A solid changing directly into a vapor undergoes which process?
Which process occurs when moth balls shrink and give off vapor without melting?
Which term describes solid-to-gas transitions?
The phase change in which a substance goes from solid to gas without passing through the liquid phase is:

questions.why: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas.
questions.deep: Deposition is the reverse (gas directly to solid, such as frost). Condensation is gas to liquid; evaporation is liquid to gas; melting is solid to liquid; freezing is liquid to solid.

variants.stem: What is the mass of 2 moles of NaCl? Use atomic masses Na = 23 and Cl = 35.5. Type a number.
Using Na = 23 and Cl = 35.5, how many grams are in 2 moles of NaCl? Type a number.
The molar mass of NaCl is the sum of Na (23) and Cl (35.5). What is the mass, in grams, of 2 moles of NaCl? Type a number.
Calculate the mass of 2.0 mol of sodium chloride (Na = 23, Cl = 35.5). Type a number.
A chemist weighs out 2 moles of table salt (NaCl). Using Na = 23 and Cl = 35.5, what is the mass in grams? Type a number.
If one mole of NaCl has a mass equal to Na (23) plus Cl (35.5), how many grams do 2 moles weigh? Type a number.
Find the mass in grams of 2 moles of NaCl given Na = 23 and Cl = 35.5. Type a number.
What is the total mass of 2 moles of NaCl? (Na = 23, Cl = 35.5) Type a number.

questions.why: Molar mass of NaCl = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 g/mol, so 2 mol × 58.5 g/mol = 117 g.
questions.deep: Mass = moles × molar mass. Always add the atomic masses of each atom in the formula to get the molar mass.

variants.stem: The reaction 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl is which type of reaction?
Two or more reactants combine to form a single product in 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl. What type of reaction is this?
Which classification fits 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl?
When elements join to form one compound, as in 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl, the reaction is a:
Which reaction type produces a single compound from simpler substances, like sodium and chlorine forming NaCl?
What kind of reaction is represented by the equation 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl?
Sodium reacts with chlorine gas to form table salt. Which reaction type does this represent?
Identify the type of reaction: 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl.

questions.why: Two reactants combining into one product is a synthesis (combination) reaction.
questions.deep: Synthesis: A + B → AB. Decomposition: AB → A + B. Single replacement: A + BC → AC + B. Double replacement: AB + CD → AD + CB.

questions.why: The dependent variable is what is measured as the outcome, here the time for the sugar to dissolve.
questions.deep: Independent = water temperature (what the student changes). Controlled variables = amount of sugar, type of cup, stirring. Dependent = what responds and is measured.

variants.stem: Which metric prefix means one-thousandth?
The prefix that represents 1/1000 of a unit is:
A milligram is one-thousandth of a gram. Which prefix means 'one-thousandth'?
Which prefix would you add to 'meter' to describe 1/1000 of a meter?
Which metric prefix stands for 0.001?
A millimeter is 1/1000 of a meter. Which prefix is that?
Which prefix is used for a factor of 10⁻³?
Which of the following prefixes indicates a unit divided by 1000?

questions.why: Milli- means one-thousandth (10⁻³).
questions.deep: Kilo = 1000, centi = 1/100, milli = 1/1000, micro = 1/1,000,000. Memory aid: 'k' goes up (kilo, bigger) while m, µ shrink the unit.

variants.stem: Which statement best describes a scientific theory?
In science, a theory is best defined as:
Which description fits the scientific meaning of 'theory'?
How do scientists use the word 'theory'?
A scientific theory is:
Which of the following correctly describes the difference between a scientific theory and a hunch?
Which choice is the correct scientific definition of a theory?
The theory of evolution and the germ theory of disease are examples of:

questions.why: A scientific theory is a well-substantiated explanation of natural phenomena supported by repeated testing and evidence.
questions.deep: A hypothesis is a testable prediction; a law describes a pattern (often mathematically); a theory explains why. Theories can be refined if new evidence appears.
